documents.title: Video Visit - acute
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt at home, ID confirmed. Two weeks of worsening breathlessness - now winded climbing the stairs to his classroom - with a dry cough and low-grade fevers at night. Home COVID antigen tests x2 negative. No chest pain. Home pulse ox in the low 90s at rest, he says, and he looks a little breathless talking.

Transplant recipient on tacrolimus/MMF/prednisone; came off PJP prophylaxis in June.

A/P: subacute dyspnea and hypoxemia in an immunosuppressed host - needs in-person evaluation and imaging today, not outpatient. Called the transplant coordinator; they want him at the transplant center ED. He has a ride. Told him to call 911 if worse on the way.

events.reason: progressive dyspnea, dry cough and low-grade fevers

medications.drug: sulfamethoxazole 800 MG / trimethoprim 160 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 2 tablets by mouth three times daily to complete 21 days of treatment

reports.text: Bilateral diffuse interstitial opacities. No lobar consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal.

documents.title: Pulmonology discharge summary
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY MEDICINE - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 1/12/2022, discharged 1/22/2022.

46M, ADPKD, deceased donor kidney 12/2020 with prior acute rejection, CMV colitis 2021. Two weeks of progressive breathlessness, nonproductive cough and low-grade fevers. Off PJP prophylaxis since 6/2021.

Arrival: afebrile, RR 28, SpO2 92% on room air. Diffuse crackles both lungs.
Labs: WBC 6.0, Hgb 13.2, plt 250, creatinine 1.5 (baseline 1.3), LDH 450 (ref 140-280). SARS-CoV-2 PCR negative.
CXR: bilateral interstitial infiltrates.
Induced sputum: routine stains and cultures negative for bacterial, viral and fungal pathogens.
Bronchoscopy with BAL 1/13: Pneumocystis jirovecii identified by direct immunofluorescence.

Dx: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia.

Course: treatment-dose TMP-SMX, supplemental O2 by nasal cannula, weaned to room air by day 6. Creatinine back to 1.3. Tacrolimus monitored.

Discharge meds: TMP-SMX DS 2 tabs TID through 2/1/2022 (21 days), then TMP-SMX SS 1 tab daily lifelong; tacrolimus 5 BID; mycophenolate 750 BID; prednisone 5; amlodipine 10; ASA 81; glargine 24; lispro per ratio. NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within a week, transplant clinic 2 weeks.

documents.title: Post-discharge visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Home 5 days after 10-day stay for PJP. Breathing much better, still tires on stairs. Cough nearly gone. No fevers. On TMP-SMX DS 2 tabs TID until 2/1, then 1 SS daily for good.

SpO2 as charted on room air. Lungs: few fine crackles at bases. Heart regular. No edema. No rash.

A/P: PJP improving. Checking K and creatinine on high-dose TMP-SMX today (transplant team wants them too; results to both). Prophylaxis restart after the course reconciled in the list. Out of school this week and next. RTC 2 months, sooner if breathing worsens.

documents.title: BMP/CBC
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: K and creatinine okay on TMP-SMX, counts fine. Forwarded to transplant clinic.

medications.drug_text: sulfamethoxazole 400 MG / trimethoprim 80 MG Oral Tablet

documents.title: Done with the big antibiotic
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Last dose of the 2-pill TMP-SMX was last night. Starting the single strength one today like the discharge sheet says. Breathing almost normal. Going back to school Monday.

documents.title: Re: Done with the big antibiotic
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great - that's right, one single-strength tablet daily from here on to keep PJP from coming back. I've updated your list. Ease back in at school.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Lungs back to normal. Busy at school, coaching the math team. Fingersticks sporadic - didn't bring his meter. Admits he sometimes skips the lunch lispro at school.
O: BP okay. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Feet intact.
A/P: DM2 - A1c today. Reviewed the lispro ratio and a simple plan for school lunches. Glargine 24 unchanged. HTN on amlodipine. PJP resolved, on SS prophylaxis. RTC 3 months.

Addendum 3/23: A1c 8.6. Portal message: let's look at numbers - asked for 2 weeks of readings; offered diabetes educator visit.

documents.title: Critical care discharge summary
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
MEDICAL ICU / HOSPITAL MEDICINE - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 7/5/2022 via ED to the ICU; transferred to the floor 7/7; discharged 7/9/2022.

46M with ADPKD, deceased donor kidney transplant with prior allograft rejection, insulin-treated type 2 diabetes. Two days of breathlessness, urinating constantly and very thirsty. Told us he had not been taking his insulin as prescribed in recent weeks.

ED: BP 130/85, HR 110, T 37.2 C. Deep, rapid respirations. Skin warm and dry.
Labs: glucose 480, HCO3 12, arterial pH 7.20, K 5.2, Na 140, Cl 95 (anion gap 33), BUN 28, Cr 1.2. Urine ketones positive. A1c 11.4.

Dx: diabetic ketoacidosis, precipitated by missed insulin.

Course: IV fluids and insulin infusion per DKA protocol with potassium monitoring; gap closed overnight, transitioned to subcutaneous glargine and lispro. Creatinine stable. Diabetes educator saw him twice. Tacrolimus continued.

Discharge meds: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin lispro 1 unit/12 g carbohydrate with meals plus correction, tacrolimus 5 BID, mycophenolate 750 BID, prednisone 5, TMP-SMX SS daily, amlodipine 10, ASA 81. NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week.

conditions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with ketoacidosis without coma

documents.title: Post-discharge visit - DKA
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 3 days after discharge for DKA. He was candid: since spring he'd been taking glargine some nights and lispro hardly ever, partly burnout after a year of hospitalizations, partly a meter that died and he never replaced. The DKA scared him.

Now: taking glargine 24 nightly and lispro with meals per ratio since discharge. Fingersticks 140-210 on the new meter. No vomiting, eating and drinking normally.

Exam: well-appearing, normal breathing. Mucous membranes moist. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
1. DKA, resolved - BMP today to confirm bicarb and K. Insulin as before; new meter and strips sent. Glucose log by portal weekly for a month.
2. DM2, A1c 11.4 - agreed plan: alarms on his phone, pen in his school bag. Educator follow-up booked.
3. Burnout - not depressed by PHQ-2 (0), but tired of being a patient. We talked about what makes the routine sustainable.
RTC 3 months with A1c; sooner if numbers stay above 250.

documents.title: Sugar log week 2
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Attached the log. Mornings 130-160, before dinner 150-200, one 240 after a cookout. Haven't missed a dose.

documents.title: Re: Sugar log week 2
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: This is a big improvement - no changes yet. Keep sending weekly through August.

reports.text: Indication: follow-up of anterior communicating artery aneurysm. Comparison 9/20/2021. Brain parenchyma normal without hemorrhage or infarct. Time-of-flight MRA: ACom aneurysm 4 mm, unchanged in size and morphology. No new aneurysm.

documents.title: MRA result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: MRA stable, 4 mm. Pt notified. Neurosurgery reviewing per their schedule.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL - 47 yo
Year: PJP admission in January (now on lifelong SS TMP-SMX), DKA in July from missed insulin. Since then steady - he's been texting logs. Transplant creatinine ~1.2. MRA in Sept stable.
Meds reviewed: tacrolimus 5 BID, MMF 750 BID, pred 5, TMP-SMX SS, amlodipine 10, ASA 81, glargine 24, lispro ratio. NKDA.
Social: teaching, smoke-free nearly 3 years, alcohol 1-2/month.
Exam: Gen well. Skin: no worrisome lesions. Lymph none. Lungs clear. CV RRR. Abd R flank fullness, graft nontender. Ext no edema. Feet: intact, pulses 2+, sensation normal.
HM: flu + bivalent COVID today. FIT kit. Derm visit for transplant skin check still not scheduled - nudged. Eye exam due.
Labs today. RTC Jan.

documents.title: A1c down
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 8.2 from 11.4. Moving the right way. Urine ACR normal. Portal note sent.

documents.title: Transplant nephrology clinic letter
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Transplant Nephrology - 11/16/2022

Nearly two years post-transplant. Interval PJP (treated, now on secondary prophylaxis) and DKA in July; doing well since. Graft function stable, creatinine at his 1.2 baseline. Tacrolimus trough 9.4. BP controlled. No edema.

Continue tacrolimus 5 mg BID, mycophenolate 750 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg, TMP-SMX SS daily. Labs every 2 months, visit in 6 months.

(FIT dropped off at our lab today for his PCP - negative, copied.)

documents.title: FIT
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: FIT negative. Next fall.

documents.title: Diabetic eye exam
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Optometry - diabetic eye examination 11/29/2022. VA 20/20 OD, 20/25 OS with correction. Dilated fundus exam: no diabetic retinopathy either eye, no macular edema. Lens clear. IOP normal. Return 1 year.

Last week of school. Sugars good, using phone reminders. No lows below 70. BP fine on amlodipine.
Exam unremarkable, feet normal.

documents.title: Dermatology skin examination
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body: Dermatology - full skin examination 8/17/2023 for organ transplant recipient surveillance. No suspicious lesions; no actinic damage requiring treatment. Counseled on daily sunscreen and sun protection. Return 1 year.

reports.text: Indication: unruptured ACom aneurysm surveillance. Comparison 9/26/2022 and 3/1/2021. Normal brain parenchyma. Time-of-flight MRA: 4 mm anterior communicating artery aneurysm without interval change. No new vascular abnormality.
reports.conclusion: Stable 4 mm ACom aneurysm over 2.5 years.

documents.title: Neurovascular surgery letter
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body: Neurovascular Surgery - imaging review 10/2023. Mr. Murphy's ACom aneurysm remains 4 mm and morphologically unchanged across three studies since March 2021. Given stability we will lengthen surveillance to MRA every 2 years. Continue blood pressure control and tobacco abstinence. Sudden severe headache warrants emergency evaluation.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. 48 yo. Quietest year since he joined - no admissions. Aneurysm stable, neurosurgery now every 2 years. Derm in August clear. Eye exam last Nov normal, due again.
Meds unchanged. NKDA.
Exam: well. Skin: no new lesions. Lungs clear. CV regular. Abd: R flank fullness, graft nontender. No edema. Feet intact.
HM: flu and updated COVID today. FIT kit. PHQ-2 0.
Labs. RTC Feb.

documents.title: Transplant nephrology clinic letter
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body: Transplant Nephrology - 11/8/2023. Almost three years out. Creatinine stable at baseline, tacrolimus 9.0, BP well controlled. No new issues. Continue tacrolimus 5 mg BID, MMF 750 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, TMP-SMX SS daily. Return 6 months.
